---
title: "Contribute"
description: "How students add and review project materials"
---

## Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sandrisper-rgb/methylation.git
cd methylation
quarto preview
```

The repository is hosted under Sandra's personal GitHub account.

## Add content

### A finding

Copy `findings/example-finding.qmd`, give it a descriptive lowercase filename, and update all metadata. Keep `draft: true` until the finding has been reviewed.

### An R workflow

Add a `.qmd` file under `workflows/`. Use relative paths, set a random seed when relevant, document packages and inputs, and confirm that no sensitive data or secrets appear in the rendered output.

### A presentation

Place the approved `.pptx` file in `presentations/files/` and add its details to `presentations.qmd`. GitHub limits individual files to 100 MB; large research artifacts belong in an approved repository rather than Git.

### An article

Add the citation to `references.bib`. Link to the DOI or legal open-access copy. Upload a PDF only if redistribution is allowed.

## Submit for review

```bash
git switch -c initials/short-description
git add path/to/changed-file
git commit -m "Add short description"
git push -u origin initials/short-description
```

Open a pull request on GitHub and request both scientific and technical review. Do not merge your own work until the team's review policy is defined.

## Local checks

```bash
quarto check
quarto render
```

Review the rendered site in `_site/`. This directory is generated and should not be committed.
